articleTitle: Metal-dielectric multilayer structure imitating epsilon-near-zero (ENZ) metamaterials: wavelength-scale electromagnetic analysis by the method of single expression
publicationTitle: International Conference on Microwave & THz Technologies, Wireless Communications and Optoelectronics (IRPhE 2024)
abstract: A wavelength-scale electromagnetic analysis is conducted on plane wave interactions in multilayer structures having permittivity in the range between zero and one, in so called epsilon-near zero (ENZ) range. For different thicknesses of such layers, along with the reflectance and transmittance analysis, the electric and magnetic field amplitude distributions within the layers are presented as well. When approaching values of the permittivity close to zero, the reflectances of layers grow significantly and high transmittance peaks are observed. Within the ENZ layer the electric field amplitude is prevailing upon the magnetic field amplitude. For imitating of ENZ artificial materials, the multi-nano-layer structure consisting of alternating positive-negative permittivity bilayers of hypothetic materials are analysed numerically. For thin enough repetitive bilayers of their relevant number the full agreement with the analysis for uniform ENZ layers is obtained. Though no real materials are specified in the current analysis, the obtained general results will be useful for designing and constructing robust ENZ multi-nano-layer structures.

articleTitle: Some peculiarities of the Schmitt trigger, inverse problem
publicationTitle: International Conference on Microwave & THz Technologies, Wireless Communications and Optoelectronics (IRPhE 2024)
abstract: New equations for solving the inverse problem of calculating Schmitt's classic triggers have been de rived, in which the threshold voltages are known as themain and invariant parameters. Dependences of relative errors of two threshold voltages on trigger output voltages and their relative errorswere derived. Graphs of this dependence were constructed. They are straight lines passing through the point of intersection of the coordinate axes. This allows one to plot these curves on a graph with just one selection of output voltage pairs and just one calculation of the relative errors of two threshold voltages.After constructing that curve, it is possible to select the pair of output voltages that will provide the smallest error in threshold voltages. The selection of all parameters and components of classical triggers is justified. Solutions have been proposed tosimultaneouslyreduce the relative errors for both thresholds in the conditions of the existing errors of output voltages. With them a new Schmitt trigger can be calculated, avoiding the errors that occur during the calculation of direct problem, when the choices of circuit parameters are not justified. Reasonable selection of parameters makes it possible to increase the quality of the triggers.

articleTitle: Beam scanning realization by a single electrically small antenna covered by magnetodielectric resonator
publicationTitle: International Conference on Microwave & THz Technologies, Wireless Communications and Optoelectronics (IRPhE 2024)
abstract: Beam scanning antennas are widely used across various applications. One instance is phased array utilizes beamformers and are characterized by their complex structures. This paper presents an innovative beam scanning technique, implemented in an electrically small microstrip patch antenna covered by a hemispherical magnetodielectric resonator. Magnetodielectric resonator impacts the performance of the microstrip patch antenna by being positioned in its reactive near-field region (Figure 1), which is designed to operate at a frequency of 13 GHz. The designed antenna exhibits a reduced frequency range (2. 5 GHz), introducing the concept of an electrically small antenna. The impedance and modal distribution of the antenna are changed by adjusting the position of the magnetodielectric (MDM) resonator relative to the microstrip antenna. The beam scanning effect is introduced as a function of frequency, differing from conventional phased array operations by contro lling the field distribution within a single antenna. Beam scanning occurs due to the excitation of higher modes of the resonator a t different frequencies with different mode distributions. Additionally, at large scanning angles, the antenna maintains a l ow side lobe level, which extends the range of the beam scanning capability.

articleTitle: Experimental determination of the binding energy of excitons in organometallic CH3NH3PbCl3-xIx perovskite films obtained by dual source vacuum thermal evaporation
publicationTitle: International Conference on Microwave & THz Technologies, Wireless Communications and Optoelectronics (IRPhE 2024)
abstract: The temperature dependences of the absorption spectra of CH<sub>3</sub>NH<sub>3</sub>PbCl<sub>3-x</sub>I<sub>x</sub>perovskite films, obtained by dual source vacuum thermal evaporation onto glass substrates with and without successively deposited ITO and TiO₂ coatings, were studied. The frequency dependence of the permittivity, the temperature dependence of the band gap, and the exciton binding energy at the temperature of 80 K were experimentally determined. It was shown that the exciton binding energy is the same for both types of samples. A calculated curve showing the fractional ratio of the concentration of free carriers to excitons as a function of photoexcitation density is also presented.

articleTitle: Characterization of microwave response of the mesh-pattern vs. uniformly-coated indium-tin-oxide indicator for the thermoelastic optical microscope: a comparative analysis
publicationTitle: International Conference on Microwave & THz Technologies, Wireless Communications and Optoelectronics (IRPhE 2024)
abstract: The microwave absorption characteristics of Hilbert-shape mesh-patterned ITO structure were examined using thermoelastic optical microscope (TEOM). Specifically, the study investigated how the distribution of the microwave electromagnetic field changes when comparing ITO indicators with mesh-pattern to those with unformal structure within the 8-12 GHz range. The findings demonstrate that by introducing certain dispersion anisotropy in the absorbing layer of the ITO indicator, both the sensitivity of the microscope and the ability to image different spatial components of the incident microwave field separatel y can be significantly enhanced. These results offer valuable insights for optimizing the microwave absorption process in the development of high-performance thermoelastic devices based on ITO films.

articleTitle: Multilayered liquid crystal systems for discrete and continuous light beam steering
publicationTitle: International Conference on Microwave & THz Technologies, Wireless Communications and Optoelectronics (IRPhE 2024)
abstract: Driving a position of light beam, i.e. light beam steering, is a rapidly growing branch of adaptive optics with applications such as light detection and ranging, imaging, optical communications, and atomic physics. For spatial scanning of light, dielectric transparent matrices with variable refractive index with quantum dots can be used a s active media, where the required phase delay is provided by a complex geometric distribution of quantum dots. Such systems are characterized by high speed and efficiency, however, their implementation requires state-of-the-art nanotechnology equipment. Having high birefringence, nematic liquid crystals (LC) are also considered as promising materials for implementation of such tasks. They are easily controlled by low-voltage electric fields, can have quite large working regions. In this work we discuss the beam steering technique by using the photo-patterned structures in a LC film as polarization diffraction gratings. To change the intensity of diffraction maxima, the light polarization is varied by an electro-optic retarder: planar LC cell with applied electric field. Combining two sets of the retarder and diffraction grating, we achieved a complex rearrangement of intensities of diffraction positions. The beam steering by electrically controlled wedge LC cells is discussed also.

articleTitle: Generation of THz radiation in a plane-parallel artificial PPLN crystal with a THz diffraction grating in output
publicationTitle: International Conference on Microwave & THz Technologies, Wireless Communications and Optoelectronics (IRPhE 2024)
abstract: In the present work, diffraction grating as an output element is proposed at the generation of terahertz radiation by optical rectification of femtosecond laser pulses in plane-parallel artificial periodically poled nonlinear crystal. The results of the simulation show the use of phase or amplitude mask as diffraction grating can obtain effective extraction of radiation from nonlinear crystal at optimal selected parameters of the mask. The crystal-to-air transmission efficiency in the presence of a phase mask is about 50 percent․ When using the proposed model, the terahertz beam emitted from the nonlinear crystal is homogeneous, in contrast to THz beams formed by other geometry at terahertz generation by optical rectification.

articleTitle: Resonant detection of surface microwaves using dielectric-coated conductive rods coupled with a cut Goubau line
publicationTitle: International Conference on Microwave & THz Technologies, Wireless Communications and Optoelectronics (IRPhE 2024)
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to mitigate dielectric and Ohmic losses in microwave frequencies and minimize signal dispersion using surface waves on wires with circular cross-sections, as discovered by Sommerfeld. While the extensive radial extension of Sommerfeld surface waves initially poses challenges due to the requirement of large isolated areas around conductors to avoid field distortion, Goubau's discovery offers a solution. By coating wires with dielectric layers, known as Goubau lines, lateral confinement of surface waves can be significantly enhanced, expanding their range of applications. These communication elements offer numerous advantages including low losses, dispersion, and simplified fabrication processes, making them ideal for ultra-wideband applications. This study investigates the resonant properties of coupled conductive rods, demonstrating their effectiveness as resonators for surface radial electromagnetic waves at microwave frequencies. The formation of standing waves is influenced by the unique distribution of radial surface waves, ensuring noticeable reflections from rod edges. Furthermore, coupling with plane microwaves polarized along the rod axis is facilitate d by the relatively weak electric field component of surface waves formed along the rod axis. The integration of double cylindrical conductive resonators with a cut Goubau line is examined, revealing sharper narrow-band resonances compared to a single rod configuration. Such resonances hold promise for practical applications as sensitive systems for monitoring ambient conditions.

articleTitle: Moving target indication as a radar cross section rapid estimate
publicationTitle: International Conference on Microwave & THz Technologies, Wireless Communications and Optoelectronics (IRPhE 2024)
abstract: An alternate method for measuring the radar cross section (RCS) of objects without relying on expensive anechoic chambers to eliminate reflections from foreign objects is proposed. In traditional radar systems, reflections from stationary objects or clutter can indeed interfere with the desired signal. The distinguishing method is based on the well-established principle of moving targets indication (MTI). By exploiting the Doppler shift we are able to filter out reflections from stationary objects, which can significantly improve the accuracy of RCS measurements, which makes it possible to effectively extract a useful signal from a uniformly moving target under test. Reflections from stationary objects can be eliminated if we place the measured object on a uniformly moving at a certain speed platform. The use of higher-order MTI filters allows for even better clutter suppression, in environments with multiple stationary objects are present.

articleTitle: Generation of THZ pulses in the transparent ferromagnetic materials by optical rectification of ultrafast laser pulses
publicationTitle: International Conference on Microwave & THz Technologies, Wireless Communications and Optoelectronics (IRPhE 2024)
abstract: In the present work, the optical rectification of femtosecond laser radiation in a transparent ferromagnetic medium was investigated. The modelling of optical rectification in the COMSOL Multiphysics environment was performed. It is shown that THz radiation can be generated by optical rectification of ultrafast laser pulses in the ferromagnetic material. THz radiation in a monocrystalline YIG was experimentally obtained by optical rectification of femtosecond laser pulses in the infrared range. The magnitude of the THz signal depends essentially on the external magnetic field and the shape of the magnetization curve of the ferromagnetic sample. This dependence is in good agreement with the static magnetization curve of the ferromagnetic sample. In the absence of an external magnetic field, the THz signal is also absent. The THz signal differs from zero at those values of the external magnetic field that correspond to the non-linear regions of the magnetization curve of the ferromagnetic sample.

articleTitle: Terahertz bandstop filter based on bilayer metasurface
publicationTitle: International Conference on Microwave & THz Technologies, Wireless Communications and Optoelectronics (IRPhE 2024)
abstract: In this work, we demonstrate through simulation calculations that a bilayer metasurface (BMS) composed of conductive rods can effectively function as a band stop filter in the terahertz frequency range. The transmittance in the 0.6 –0.9 THz range is approximately 2% or less, which implies a bandwidth of 0.3 THz and a central frequency of 0.75 THz. The characteristics (bandwidth, central frequency, transition band and etc.) of proposed structure can be finely tuned by altering its geometric parameters, such as the diameter and length of rods, the periodicity, and the distance between the layers. The developed terahertz filter may have significant potential for applications in terahertz communications, sensors, and other emerging terahertz technologies.

articleTitle: Investigation of structural and optical properties of CsPbBr3films synthesized by single-source vacuum evaporation method
publicationTitle: International Conference on Microwave & THz Technologies, Wireless Communications and Optoelectronics (IRPhE 2024)
abstract: In this study, with the use of X-ray diffraction, optical microscopy imaging and optical spectrophotometric techniques, we investigated influence of the thermal annealing regime on structural and optical properties of CsPbBr3 perovskite polycrystalline films deposited by single-source vacuum thermal evaporation method. The process of the thermal annealing was conducted in ambient air at temperatures of 250°C, 275°C, and 300°C for annealing time of 60 min. It is obtained that both as-deposited and annealed films are composed of pure CsPbBr3 perovskite phase with orthorhombic structure. The process of annealing resulted in drastic improvement of the degree of crystallinity and strong coarsening of grains in the films. Increase of the annealing temperature resulted in monotonic increase of the average size of crystallites (coherent crystallographic domains) and grains. Formation of a strong texture is revealed in CsPbBr3 films annealed at 275°C and 300°C, and this is attributed to a strong coarsening of grains owing to their sintering. The decrease of the optical absorbance in the films with increase of the annealing temperature is attributed to decrease of the densities of grain boundaries and absorbing point defects. For all examined CsPbBr3 films the optical band gap is determined to be the same, 2.34 eV.

articleTitle: Application of Bessel beams for radio communication
publicationTitle: International Conference on Microwave & THz Technologies, Wireless Communications and Optoelectronics (IRPhE 2024)
abstract: Diffraction phenomena are characteristic properties of wave propagation that arise from the obstruction of propagating waves. In this article, we discuss the properties of Bessel beams, which are inherently quite stable against diffraction. It is demonstrated that the stability of Bessel beams against obstacles is represented by the characteristics of the J<sub>0</sub>and J<sub>1</sub>beams.

articleTitle: Thermoelectric single photon detector for far UV radiation with THz count rate
publicationTitle: International Conference on Microwave & THz Technologies, Wireless Communications and Optoelectronics (IRPhE 2024)
abstract: We present the results of modeling of heat propagation processes in thermoelectric sensors after absorption of single UV photons with 7.1 eV energy. Thermoelectric multilayer sensors with an operating temperature of 1 K consist of a tungsten absorber, a thermoelectric layer of La<sub>0.99</sub>Ce<sub>0.01</sub>B<sub>6</sub>, a tungsten heat sink and a dielectric substrate of Al<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub>. Modeling and simulation of heat transfer processes in thermoelectric sensors with different layer thicknesses and surface areas was carrie d out using the three-dimensional matrix method for differential equations based on the equation of heat propagation from a limited volume. The temporal dependencies of the temperature at various areas of the sensors and the average temperature of the layers’ surfaces were calculated. The patterns obtained allow us to propose an optimal design for thermoelectric sensors. For the thermoelectric sensor with surface area of 1 and 4 μm<sup>2</sup>, absorber and thermoelectric layer thicknesses of 40 and 10 nm respectively, the FWHM of signal is 0.196 ps. Corresponding count rate of thermoelectric sensor equal to 5.1 THz.

articleTitle: Statistical analysis of the electroencephalographic signals
publicationTitle: International Conference on Microwave & THz Technologies, Wireless Communications and Optoelectronics (IRPhE 2024)
abstract: In this work, radio signals received from the brain (in the frequency range up to several tens of megahertz) were recorded using various sensors and their statistical (in particular, spectral and bispectral) analysis was performed. Analyses were performed in the LabVIEW environment using the Advanced Signal Processing Toolkit. It is shown that by means of bispectral analysis, it is possible to distinguish such spectral components of the registered biosignals, which are statistically related to each other, and in addition are somewhat correlated with the mental and physical states of a person. Based on the results of spectral and bispectral analysis of the signals received from the sensors, a system was developed, through which the non-informative components of these signals are pre-filtered, due to which disturbances are reduced, and therefore the effectiveness of the statistical analysis of the signals is increased.

articleTitle: More accurate and effective monitoring of moving targets in complex environments using "spectral mask" for harmonic signatures using higher-ordered statistics
publicationTitle: International Conference on Microwave & THz Technologies, Wireless Communications and Optoelectronics (IRPhE 2024)
abstract: In signal processing and target detection, bispectral analysis provides a robust framework for identifying and characterising non-linear interactions and harmonic relationships in time series data. This paper presents an innovative approach to bispectral analysis customised for moving targets, utilizing spectral masks to improve the detection of harmonic frequencies. Our method involves the creation of a spectral mask that selectively amplifies the desired harmonics within the bispectrum, effectively reducing noise and other irrelevant signals. This targeted approach enhances the resolution and clarity of harmonic signatures, facilitating improved tracking and characterization of moving targets. We validate the effectiveness of our approach through simulations and real-world scenarios, demonstrating significant enhancements in target detection performance and frequency resolution compared to traditional bispectral analysis methods. The proposed technique paves the way for advanced signal processing applications, particularly in radar and sonar systems, where precise target tracking and classification are crucial. By refining the bispectral analysis process and concentrating on harmonic frequencies, our method contributes to more accurate and efficient monitoring of moving targets in complex environments.

articleTitle: CdS thin films grown on polyimide plastic substrate by chemical bath deposition
publicationTitle: International Conference on Microwave & THz Technologies, Wireless Communications and Optoelectronics (IRPhE 2024)
abstract: Polycrystalline cadmium sulfide (CdS) thin films were deposited onto polyimide (PI) plastic substrates by chemical bath technique at fixed solution temperature (62±1)C. We report the effect of deposition time on the structural and optical properties of as deposited thin films. The X-ray diffraction (XRD) results showed that the deposited films are mainly consisting of hexagonal CdS phase and the crystallite size was about 10 nm and slightly decreased with deposition time. Scanning electron micrographs show homogeneous, compact and smooth surface of films. The Raman measurements revealed three main peaks corresponding to the 1LO, 2LO, and 3LO modes of CdS. The optical band gap values of CdS films slightly increased as the deposition time increases, and it was found to be in the range of 2.30-2.37 eV. The results demonstrate that the deposition of CdS from chemical bath on PI substrates at the low temperature without need any post-deposition treatment can result in improved physical properties of the films and paves the way to integrate CdS thin films in flexible optoelectronic devices.

articleTitle: 2D MoS2phototransistor deposited on a flexible substrate
publicationTitle: International Conference on Microwave & THz Technologies, Wireless Communications and Optoelectronics (IRPhE 2024)
abstract: A new phototransistor, utilizing a bi-layer of MoS2deposited on a polyimide substrate, has been successfully fabricated through the pulsed-laser deposition technique. It has been shown that the photo-responsivity of the device can be adjusted over a wide range by controlling the gate and drain voltages. In response to the pulsed illumination, the structure shows a switching behavior with the characteristic time about tens of ms. The photocurrent has been found to vary considerably due to compressive or tensile strain induced by bended substrate that affects the band-gap of ultrathin MoS2 layers.

articleTitle: Antireflectivity and diffuse scattering from rough surfaces
publicationTitle: International Conference on Microwave & THz Technologies, Wireless Communications and Optoelectronics (IRPhE 2024)
abstract: Antireflectivity is crucial for optimizing the efficiency of solar cells. Achieving effective anti-reflection with high-refractive-index materials is challenging due to their inherently high reflectivity, as described by Fresnel equations. Recent research has explored the potential of nanorough surfaces—where the roughness parameters are much smaller than the wavelength of incident light. This focus has shifted with the advent of modern theoretical approaches that incorporate modified boundary conditions. Our study examines weakly rough opaque surfaces and demonstrates significant differences in predictions for specular and diffuse scattering compared to older theories. These findings are validated by experimental results on nano-roughened silicon films across wavelengths of 300-400 nm. At this part of the spectrum, the reflection is shown to decrease significantly, which opens new possibilities for solar cell technology to harness energy from previously inaccessible regions of the spectrum.

articleTitle: Investigation of nonlinear properties of animal spinal cord in THZ range
publicationTitle: International Conference on Microwave & THz Technologies, Wireless Communications and Optoelectronics (IRPhE 2024)
abstract: In the present work the electrodynamic properties of a system consisting of animal spinal cord nerve fibres in the terahertz range (0.1-3 THz) are experimentally investigated using time domain spectrometer. It is shown that when an external constant voltage is applied to the sample, significant changes in the parameters of the spinal cord sample (refractive index, absorption) occur when the electric field vector of the terahertz radiation is oriented parallel to the nerve fibres. A model was proposed, according to which under the influence of a voltage greater than threshold, the opening of the channels of nodes of Ranvier of the nerve fibres occurs, due to which the nerve fibres are transformed into specific wires with nonlinear conductivity, and the entire sample into a diffraction grating consisting of these wires. Computer modelling of the nonlinear interaction of THz radiation with the spinal cord sample was performed, the results of which are in good agreement with the experimentally obtained results.

articleTitle: Design and preparation of the adaptive direction-finding system for using the smart jamming RF signals systems in the 1-6 GHz frequency range
publicationTitle: International Conference on Microwave & THz Technologies, Wireless Communications and Optoelectronics (IRPhE 2024)
abstract: The rapid development of wireless communication technologies has required the use of advanced methods of protection and management of the radio frequency (RF) spectrum. Jamming is the most important method of interrupting unauthorized or malicious communications, but traditional methods are often inaccurate and can interfere with legitimate users. The purpose of this work is to design and develop a smart RF jamming system that includes an adaptive direction-finding component to improve accuracy and minimize unintended interference. The proposed system uses an amplitude comparison method that measures the strength of a signal received by several spatially spaced antennas. Adaptive algorithms allow real-time correction of the direction of the suppressed signal to the target source. The experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the system in accurately targeting and suppressing certain signals, minimizing interference to non-targeted messages. The system demonstrates significant improvements in efficiency and strategic application in scenarios such as electronic warfare, security operations and the protection of critical infrastructure. The developed smart RF jamming system using adaptive direction finding represents significant progress in radio frequency spectrum management and safety. It is a practical and effective tool for precise and effective jamming in an era of sophisticated wireless communications.

articleTitle: On a Bessel function integral which occurs in electronic thin film theory
publicationTitle: International Conference on Microwave & THz Technologies, Wireless Communications and Optoelectronics (IRPhE 2024)
abstract: The aim of this paper is to investigate the salient features of a Bessel function involving integral which plays a well known role in the theory of screened Coulomb interactions in thin semiconductor films. We present a method for an exact analytical evaluation of this parameter-dependent integral in the regime of strong electronic screening. The transformation properties of calculated integral in the complex variable plane are discussed.

articleTitle: SC-DSB signal as a probe signal for testing nonlinearity in electronic circuits
publicationTitle: International Conference on Microwave & THz Technologies, Wireless Communications and Optoelectronics (IRPhE 2024)
abstract: In today's technological landscape, there is a growing reliance on wireless devices for a wide range of applications, spannin g from data networks to wireless sensors. In order to identify and analyze these wireless devices, it is crucial to conduct thorough surveys of the surrounding environment. However, this task becomes challenging when it comes to characterizing the properties of the RF circuit. When a two-dimensional signal is transmitted to an RF device, it is impacted by the nonlinear components of the circuit, such as amplifiers and diodes. These nonlinear components give rise to intermodulation distortion of the input signal, which is then re-radiated by the device [1]. The characteristics of the intermodulation distortion result are harnessed to construct a unique fingerprint of the device [1]. This fingerprint is subsequently utilized to effectively characterize the device, enabling its identification among other RF devices.
